name: Helmet
label: AmRep
lede: Four guys in sneakers, one label that survived on a $2,500 record, and a major-label bidding war that made 'Meantime' the loudest short-haired album of 1992.

eras.title: Four guys, no hair gel, one Minneapolis label
eras.text: Page Hamilton leaves Band of Susans and builds the tightest, plainest band on the Lower East Side. A Minneapolis noise-rock label hears it, and a 1990 record made for $2,500 keeps that label alive for the decade.

years.h: Page Hamilton leaves Band of Susans and starts Helmet
years.p: [[Page Hamilton|c3aa624f-9b04-4414-b3f0-1f844d165440]], who came up around [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]]'s guitar ensembles and [[Band of Susans|12858790-851b-4899-ac07-9ac6373cf133]], forms the band in New York with bassist [[Henry Bogdan|1b854c5b-5b07-4c1d-b5ad-61abe484e1f1]], guitarist [[Peter Mengede|b2d7a5e6-c790-4e17-b413-9e4d2f9d225a]] and drummer [[John Stanier|4d81d3a6-b6f2-42ba-b93c-348b73097080]].

years.h: The name comes from a mishearing
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Mengede's then-wife Reyne Cuccuro suggested "Helmuth", and Hamilton heard it as the thing you wear on your head.
years.xp: The story goes that the band got a name by accident, and a very un-metal one. Helmet would spend its career being mistaken for a metal band anyway.

years.h: [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] signs them: the "Born Annoying" 7-inch
years.p: Amphetamine Reptile Records founder Tom Hazelmyer, who also played guitar in Halo of Flies, releases Helmet's first single, "Born Annoying".

years.src: Wikipedia: Strap It On · Wikipedia: Amphetamine Reptile Records
years.h: Strap It On made for $2,500 at Fun City
years.p: Recorded in New York with Wharton Tiers and released on Amphetamine Reptile, it is all stop-start riffs and no solos.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, it was recorded at Fun City in New York for $2,500, produced by Wharton Tiers and the band. It reportedly sold around 10,000 copies by September 1992.

By February 1995 that figure had grown to 40,000. Hazelmyer has said the record helped support the other things on the label that sold less, which is how AmRep got through the 1990s.

years.cap: Helmet3 The Hifi Bar, Melbourne May 2008 · Wikimedia
years.h: CBGB in 1990: the band before the bidding war
years.p: A 1990 CBGB set was later released as part of the 2021 archive collection Live and Rare, so you can hear how tight they already were.
years.xp: According to the Tidal magazine piece on Meantime at 30, the 2021 release Live and Rare collects a 1990 CBGB performance alongside a post-Meantime Big Day Out set.

eras.title: The next Nirvana auction
eras.text: After Nirvana, every A&R person in America wants a loud guitar band from the underground. Helmet gets a bidding war, a huge contract and a record that turns a reversed hard-rock cliché into a hit.

years.h: Interscope wins the bidding war for Helmet
years.p: Following a publicized scramble among labels after Nirvana, Helmet signs with Interscope Records for three albums, with unusual creative control.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the deal at a $1.2 million advance across three records, plus $50,000 in tour support. The Meantime album page instead says approximately $1 million, so the exact figure is not settled.

Amphetamine Reptile kept vinyl distribution rights on the Interscope deal, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Meantime is recorded in New York and Chicago for $25,000
years.p: Wharton Tiers engineers at Fun City in New York; [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] works on the title track at CRC in Chicago; [[Andy Wallace|665695c1-d546-4141-8dd7-1cd40a1eea71]] mixes.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the recording window as December 1991 to February 1992, with the budget at $25,000 and Helmet as producers. Tidal notes Albini had first done demo work on "In the Meantime".

years.h: Meantime arrives, with "Unsung" as the calling card
years.p: Interscope's first Helmet record was pushed back from April; it hits #1 on the Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits three singles with videos: "Unsung", "In the Meantime" (June 8, 1992) and "Give It". The album peaked at #68 on the Billboard 200 and was certified gold in 1994.

The cover uses a steel-mill photograph by David Plowden, and there were two reversible colour variants.

years.big: Sneakers, jeans, short hair. On Beavis and Butt-Head, that was the joke.
q: That drummer looks like a regular guy.
years.h: "That drummer looks like a regular guy"
years.p: Helmet's plain look, refusing the long hair of metal, got name-checked on the MTV cartoon.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes that the band rejected metal's traditional look for t-shirts, jeans, sneakers and short haircuts. A Beavis and Butt-Head episode has the pair commenting on it.

years.h: Interscope reissues Strap It On
years.p: The 1990 debut gets a major-label re-release in January 1993, so kids who bought Meantime can hear where it started.

q: Money kind of came in and changed things.
years.h: [[Peter Mengede|b2d7a5e6-c790-4e17-b413-9e4d2f9d225a]] leaves over contract disputes
years.p: According to Wikipedia, the second guitarist departs early in 1993 after disputes over the deal; he later joins Handsome.
years.xp: Wikipedia says he left over contractual disputes and went on to Handsome, whose one album came out on Epic. Hamilton, asked about the classic lineup's collapse, told Blabbermouth that money "kind of came in and changed things".

years.h: [[Rob Echeverria|0b8b2179-3147-4736-acbf-8e44d75d1557]] takes over on guitar
years.p: The former Rest in Pieces guitarist steps into Mengede's spot.

years.h: "Just Another Victim" with House of Pain
years.p: Helmet teams with rap group House of Pain on a track for the Judgment Night soundtrack, a film built around rock and rap pairings.

eras.title: Jazz chords, a hit in a crow's shadow
eras.text: With the pressure on, Hamilton writes a colder, stranger record. Interscope's push fades fast, but one single ends up on a major movie soundtrack.

years.h: Betty: jazz and blues chords in a Helmet riff
years.p: Produced by T-Ray and [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] at three New York studios, it peaks at #45 on the Billboard 200, their highest.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the band experimented with jazz and blues influences; Hamilton has called those his indulgences. "Milquetoast" became the biggest hit and appeared on The Crow soundtrack.

It sold about 500,000 copies worldwide by 1997, less than Meantime, and Interscope's promotional support faded quickly. Rolling Stone later put it in its 2014 list of 1994's best records.

years.cap: Helmet in The Jerky Boys: The Movie
years.h: Helmet plays Black Sabbath in The Jerky Boys movie
years.p: They cover Black Sabbath's "Symptom of the Universe" on screen, with Ozzy Osbourne in a cameo as manager.

years.h: Rob Echeverria leaves for Biohazard
years.p: According to Wikipedia, this exit is far friendlier than Mengede's; he joins [[Biohazard|be5fe2ab-007c-4610-8d53-d81675d06a09]].

eras.title: Three guys, one guitar, 1,600 shows
eras.text: Down to a trio, Helmet finishes an album, rejects the mix, remixes it and tours with the new nu-metal generation. Then the classic lineup falls apart.

years.h: Aftertaste arrives after a scrapped mix
years.p: A first mix by Dave Sardy is rejected; Terry Date remixes it, and the track "Renovation" is added.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the record was nearly done in late 1996 when the mix was withdrawn after promotion had started. It debuted at #47 on the Billboard 200 and had sold 132,000 copies by 2004. Hamilton plays all the guitar; [[Chris Traynor|80f36457-d56f-4444-a750-cc52bfb77f00]] joins for the tour.

years.h: Chris Traynor joins for a tour with Korn, Limp Bizkit and Melvins
years.p: The Orange 9mm guitarist fills out the live band for the Aftertaste run.

years.cap: Helmet, late in the original run
years.h: Helmet call it quits after 1,600 shows
years.p: Their last show of the era was December 10, 1997 in Italy; the breakup was made official in November 1998.
years.xp: Hamilton's statement, per Wikipedia, tallied nine years, 1,600 shows and five albums. He told Blabbermouth later that money had changed the band's chemistry and that he struggled with the guilt of being the main writer.

eras.title: Bowie, Battles and a long quiet
eras.text: The members scatter into unusual company.

years.h: Page Hamilton plays guitar with [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]]
years.p: Hamilton toured with Bowie in 1999 and wrote film music alongside composer Elliot Goldenthal.
years.xp: He also played in a guitar orchestra, Deaf Elk, and kept a New York band called Gandhi, whose songs fed later Helmet records.

years.p: The drummer joins [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]]'s Tomahawk, and later Battles.

eras.title: Same name, new band, wrong label
eras.text: Hamilton reforms Helmet as a working band with new players. Interscope drops it, and Warcon leaves him unpaid.

years.h: Size Matters is Hamilton's record, not the band's
years.p: Stanier and Bogdan declined to return; John Tempesta plays drums and Chris Traynor bass.
years.xp: Wikipedia says its release slid from September 14 after Hamilton broke his collarbone mountain biking. Lyrics drew on his year with actress Winona Ryder. It debuted at #121 on the Billboard 200 with 9,723 copies in week one.

years.h: Interscope drops Helmet after Size Matters
years.p: Poor sales end the label relationship that began in 1992.

years.h: Monochrome comes out on Warcon
years.p: Recorded with early producer Wharton Tiers, the album is followed by tour-support money the label never paid, Hamilton says.
years.xp: Hamilton said he never got royalties or tour support from Warcon, but now owns the record.

years.h: Helmet open for Guns N' Roses
years.p: A late-year tour on which the band starts to look stable again.

eras.title: Still here
eras.text: A steady band, and a slow return to respect.

years.h: Seeing Eye Dog is Helmet's seventh album
years.p: Hamilton, Kyle Stevenson, Dan Beeman and Dave Case make up the line-up that holds for the next decade.

years.h: Meantime played in full across Europe
years.p: A 28-show European tour has the band playing the album front to back; Peter Mengede briefly returns onstage in Brisbane.

years.h: Dead to the World: the eighth record
years.p: Follows the single "Bad News"; the same year a hardcore tribute, Meantime Redux, appears.

years.h: Helmet celebrate 30 years
years.p: Anniversary tours run through Europe, North America, then New Zealand and Australia in 2020.

years.h: Left, the ninth album, with "Holiday" first
years.p: Lead single "Holiday" appears in August; the album follows on November 10.

years.h: A Betty anniversary and a cancelled Local H run
years.p: The tour with Local H is called off and moved to February-March 2025.
